findings.title: The warning calls POST and PATCH "an unsafe method", but retrylint warns on non-idempotent methods (RFC 9110, section 9.2.2), and PUT and DELETE, which are unsafe too, get no warning.
findings.problem: RFC 9110 defines "safe" (section 9.2.1: GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) and "idempotent" (section 9.2.2: those plus PUT and DELETE) as different properties. A user who knows the RFC reads the warning as stating the rule, then finds retried PUT and DELETE endpoints in the same file passing without a word; a user who does not learns the wrong rule. The warning is the only text in the project that names the rule this way, and the description, which claims only a shorter message with the endpoint and the count first, does not claim a change of reason.

evidence.text: retrylint/messages.py:6: `f"{file}:{endpoint.line}: {endpoint.method} {endpoint.path} => retry x{endpoint.retries} on an unsafe method; "`

retrylint/__main__.py:7-9: "RFC 9110, section 9.2.2 defines GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, and DELETE as idempotent"; `IDEMPOTENT = {"GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "TRACE", "PUT", "DELETE"}`; retrylint/__main__.py:16 warns only `if endpoint.retries > 0 and endpoint.method not in IDEMPOTENT`.

README.md:19-20: "it is only harmless for a method that RFC 9110 defines as idempotent (section 9.2.2): GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT, and DELETE. POST and PATCH are not idempotent." The README is unchanged by the commit, and no file at the base uses the word "safe".
tests/golden/put_delete_retry.conf retries PUT 5 times and DELETE 2 times, and tests/golden/put_delete_retry.txt expects no warning.

Removed text: `but {endpoint.method} is not idempotent (RFC 9110, section 9.2.2)`. Commit 7463fb4b body: "Put them first and keep the message short enough to scan in a CI log." No sentence mentions the reason the warning gives.

Run at the head on `PUT /orders/42 5`, `DELETE /orders/42 2`, `POST /orders 1`, `LOCK /x 2`: only lines 3 and 4 are reported, as `p.conf:3: POST /orders => retry x1 on an unsafe method; a retry may apply its effect twice. Drop the retry policy.`

With the suggestion applied, `python3 -m retrylint tests/golden/post_retry.conf` prints the line quoted in proposed_solution, and the LOCK line of the run above reads `p.conf:4: LOCK /x has retries set to 2, but LOCK is not idempotent, so a retried request may apply its effect twice. Set retries to 0.` Source lines are 112 and 114 characters, within the 120 the other modules keep.

findings.proposed_solution:
Name the property the check tests. The suggestion rewrites both lines of the message, because a text that changes only the term still fails F2, F3, and F5 (same class); it keeps the endpoint and the count first. Rendered for tests/golden/post_retry.conf:

`tests/golden/post_retry.conf:3: POST /orders has retries set to 3, but POST is not idempotent, so a retried request may apply its effect twice. Set retries to 0.`

and for tests/golden/patch_retry.conf:

`tests/golden/patch_retry.conf:1: PATCH /orders/42 has retries set to 2, but PATCH is not idempotent, so a retried request may apply its effect twice. Set retries to 0.`

Update tests/golden/post_retry.txt and tests/golden/patch_retry.txt to these lines.

reproducer.code:
printf 'PUT /orders/42 5\nPOST /orders 3\n' > c.conf
python3 -m retrylint c.conf
# current:  c.conf:2: POST /orders => retry x3 on an unsafe method; ...  (PUT, also unsafe, is not reported)
# expected: the warning gives the reason the check uses: POST is not idempotent

findings.suggestion:
f"{file}:{endpoint.line}: {endpoint.method} {endpoint.path} has retries set to {endpoint.retries}, but "
        f"{endpoint.method} is not idempotent, so a retried request may apply its effect twice. Set retries to 0."
findings.retest: The warnings for tests/golden/post_retry.conf and tests/golden/patch_retry.conf say the method is not idempotent ("not idempotent" or "non-idempotent") and do not contain "unsafe"; the warning for a method outside the IDEMPOTENT set that the goldens do not cover, such as `LOCK /x 2`, uses the same wording; tests/golden/put_delete_retry.conf still prints nothing.

findings.title: "Drop the retry policy" uses the project's name for the whole policy file to mean the retries of one endpoint.
findings.problem: Read in the README's sense, the advice is to remove the retries of every endpoint, the GET, PUT, and DELETE ones included, or the file itself; the check passes once this endpoint's retries are 0.

evidence.text: retrylint/messages.py:7: `f"a retry may apply its effect twice. Drop the retry policy."`
README.md:3: "`retrylint` checks the retry policy of an HTTP client before it ships. A policy file lists one endpoint per line"; retrylint/policy.py:1: "Reads a retry policy file."

retrylint/__main__.py:16 warns only when `endpoint.retries > 0`; tests/golden/patch_retry.conf:2 `POST /payments 0` gets no warning. The column is named `retries` in README.md:7 and tests/golden/post_retry.conf:1 (`# method path retries`).
Removed text: "Remove the retry, or send an Idempotency-Key header that the server deduplicates."

The Idempotency-Key remedy need not come back into the warning: the policy file has no column for it, so an endpoint that follows it keeps its warning, and retries set to 0 is the one remedy the check accepts. Its removal is a user-visible change the description does not mention (F4).

findings.proposed_solution: F1's suggestion renders the remedy as `Set retries to 0.` after `POST /orders has retries set to 3`, which resolves this finding. If F1 is fixed by changing only the term on line 6, this finding stays, and line 7 still points the remedy at the whole policy.
findings.retest: The remedy in the warnings for tests/golden/post_retry.conf and tests/golden/patch_retry.conf names the reported endpoint's retries and a value the check accepts (0), and does not contain "retry policy".

findings.title: The warning invents the notation `=> retry x3`, which neither RFC 9110, the README, nor retrylint's other output uses, and `x3` does not say whether 3 counts retries or attempts.
findings.problem: A user cannot look up what `=>` relates. The policy column counts retries after the first request, so `retry x3` means up to four sends, while `x3` in a CI log reads as easily as three sends in total; a user who compares it with a max-attempts setting is off by one.

evidence.text: retrylint/messages.py:6: `{endpoint.method} {endpoint.path} => retry x{endpoint.retries}`; tests/golden/post_retry.txt:1 renders `POST /orders => retry x3`.

README.md:3-4: the third column is "how many times the client retries a failed request". Neither `=>` nor an `xN` count appears in the repository at the base. Removed text: "is retried up to {endpoint.retries} times".

findings.proposed_solution: F1's suggestion renders `POST /orders has retries set to 3`, which names the count by the policy column and also reads correctly for 1 (`has retries set to 1`, where the base wording gave `retried up to 1 times`). If F1 is fixed by changing only the term, this finding stays, and line 6 still needs the count written in words.

reproducer.code:
printf 'POST /orders 1\n' > c.conf
python3 -m retrylint c.conf
# current:  c.conf:1: POST /orders => retry x1 on an unsafe method; ...
# expected: the count stated in words as a number of retries, without `=>` or `x1`

findings.retest: The warnings for tests/golden/post_retry.conf and tests/golden/patch_retry.conf contain neither `=>` nor an `x<digits>` token and state the count as a number of retries; the warning for `POST /orders 1` does the same and does not read "1 times".

findings.title: The commit message gives the 80-column wrap as the problem, but the new warning still wraps, and it does not say that the RFC citation and the Idempotency-Key remedy were removed.
findings.problem: A reader of the commit takes the wrap as fixed and the warning's advice as unchanged. The text after the `file:line:` prefix alone is 104 characters for `POST /orders`, so no file name makes the warning fit in 80 columns.

evidence.text: Commit 7463fb4b body: "The warning wrapped over three lines in an 80-column terminal, and the endpoint and the retry count sat in the middle of it. Put them first and keep the message short enough to scan in a CI log."

Line lengths at the head: tests/golden/patch_retry.txt:1 is 141 characters, tests/golden/post_retry.txt:1 is 136. The base tests/golden/post_retry.txt:1 was 303 characters, four lines at 80 columns, not three.
Removed text: "(RFC 9110, section 9.2.2)" and "or send an Idempotency-Key header that the server deduplicates"; the body mentions neither.

findings.proposed_solution: Reword the body to the outcome the change keeps: the endpoint and the retry count come first and the warning is shorter. Drop the 80-column claim unless the final warning fits, and name the removed RFC citation and Idempotency-Key remedy with the reason they went, against the wording that F1 settles.
findings.retest: The commit message implies the warning fits in 80 columns only where the rendered warning does, and it names every part of the old warning that the final text drops.

findings.title: "a retry may apply its effect twice" gives the effect to the retry; it is the retried request's effect that may be applied twice.

evidence.text: Removed text: "a retried request may apply its effect twice"; retrylint/messages.py:7: "a retry may apply its effect twice". RFC 9110, section 9.2.2 speaks of the effect on the server of multiple identical requests.

findings.proposed_solution: F1's suggestion renders `so a retried request may apply its effect twice`, which resolves this finding. If F1 is fixed by changing only the term, this finding stays on line 7.
findings.retest: The rendered warning says that the retried request, not the retry, may apply its effect twice.

classes.title: The shortened warning coins its own words
classes.root_cause: The rewrite of non_idempotent_retry replaced the words the README, the policy file, and RFC 9110 use (not idempotent, retries, the retried request) with new terms and notation, so one rewrite of retrylint/messages.py:6-7 in those words fixes F1, F2, F3, and F5.
